newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle close mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle close mostly higher.

text.p: Firmer cash fed cattle markets kept the nearby CME live cattle futures supported at the close despite rolling of longs, traders said.

Fed cattle selling at $66.00 per cwt, up $1 from earlier in the week, provided the bulk of support. Expectations that cash beef and fed markets will remain strong into the new year also provided support, traders said.

Early rolling of long positions into April came on anticipation that funds would roll their positions about two weeks from now. With holidays cutting the amount of time, longs were willing to roll positions early, they said.

Some scattered profit taking was also cited after the runup following higher cash markets. However, overall trade activity remained light due to the holiday period and release of the quarterly USDA Hogs and Pigs Report Friday afternoon, they added.
Refco was a notable buyer early while E.D.&F. Man and RBH sold, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, February volatility was down about one percent on commercial selling of 64 to 66 calls, pit sources added.

Feeder cattle recovered from early losses in thin dealings following the retreat in corn futures. Deferred months showed the most strength on scattered demand which lifted May through November to new contract highs, traders said.

Expectations that feed costs will remain low and feeder cattle supplies will tighten by next fall lifted deferreds into scattered buy stops. Spreaders also bought deferred feeders against short nearby cattle positions, they said.

Refco bought May feeders after Cargill Investor Services lightly bought January and March on the early scale down. Paine Webber spread long August short April and Cargill bought August and sold December live cattle. Cargill also spread long June live cattle/short January feeders, pit sources said.
The latest CME index was off $0.11 at $65.45 per cwt.
Live cattle closed 0.125 cent higher to 0.100 lower with February up 0.075 at 65.025 cents. Feeder cattle ended off 0.125 to up 0.400 with January off 0.125 at 66.950 cents.
